messages:
alex: Took a short spike on a manifest-based snapshot approach for prefix ownership in the KV cache. TL;DR: keep a small, versioned manifest per shard that lists prefix->owner, snapshot_id, and a compact diff for moves. Question: does this simplify correctness for compaction + eviction or just add complexity?

maria: quick question — how is this different from the epoched-lease model we already have?

alex: Good call. Differences: the manifest is append-only metadata that describes placement snapshots (like a mini-CRDT), not a transient lease. Key points: 1) manifest is durable and versioned (manifest_vN). 2) owners apply diffs to move prefixes; diffs are idempotent because they're tagged with manifest_v and op_id. 3) reads consult active_manifest then local residency for fast path. That avoids having to coordinate a fencing lease handshake for every handoff.

jonathan: Concern: compaction + background eviction can reorder tombstone application. How do reads see a consistent state when a prefix is moved mid-compaction?

alex: Plan: when applying a manifest move we attach a small quiesce window: new_owner gets a snapshot_id and records `applied_until` for that snapshot. Any read with snapshot_id <= applied_until must consult the old-owner tombstone set. Implementation sketch: store (prefix, manifest_v, applied_until_ts) in the manifest. Reads check: if local manifest_v < requested manifest_v and ts <= applied_until -> route read to prior owner or consult tombstone cache.

lee: That feels like adding another routing hop for some reads. What's the perf hit? Also eviction: if the old owner evicted entries because of memory pressure, how do we prevent stale reads?

alex: Perf hit is limited because quiesce windows are tiny (seconds) and we expect most moves to be prefilled by the new owner. For eviction safety we add a compact tombstone bloom: small in-memory bloom per-prefix of recent deletions (3-5KB) that survives eviction. New owner checks bloom before accepting a read as a fresh miss. If bloom says maybe-deleted -> consult prior owner or rehydrate.

maria: Bloom + manifest sounds reasonable. Is there an invariant we can assert to detect violations in prod?

jonathan: We can instrument a checksum compare: once per minute, pick a random prefix that moved recently and compare a small fingerprint (e.g., CRC32 of first N keys) between old and new owner — if mismatch, alert. Cheap and catches reorder bugs.

alex: love that. Also propose a runtime invariant: for any prefix p, any read that returns a value v must satisfy one of: (a) owner manifest_v equals read manifest_v, or (b) bloom indicated possible tombstone and return was verified by prior owner. We can emit an event when invariant fails.

lee: Edge-case: what about long-lived cursors that hold a handle across a move? Those still expect monotonic reads.

alex: For long cursors we issue a stable cursor token tied to a manifest_v and snapshot_id. If manifest_v advances beyond token + tolerance, cursor must be fast-failed with a specific retry code so client can re-acquire. We avoid transparent migration for long-lived cursors for now.

jonathan: How does this interact with our existing fallback policy (model routing -> cheaper variant)? If manifest routing is strict, fallback might go to a different slab that doesn't have tombstones.

alex: Fallback policy should prefer the last-known owner for a short grace window. After that, it can fall back to cheaper variant but must mark the response as stale-possible. We'll add a response header `x-prefix-origin: owner|fallback|stale-possible`.

alex: Pushed a tiny prototype branch: https://git.internal/r/redwood/kv-manifest-spike (contains manifest proto and apply loop). Example log from prototype:
```
[2025-10-12T14:22:01Z] manifest_apply v12: move prefix "usr:123" -> node-7 op=op-47
[2025-10-12T14:22:02Z] node-7 prefill started for prefix "usr:123" snapshot_id=12
[2025-10-12T14:22:03Z] node-3 bloom export for "usr:123" size=3584 bytes
[2025-10-12T14:22:04Z] node-7 manifest_v=12 applied_until=2025-10-12T14:22:06Z
```

maria: Nice logs. Can we run chaos tests that: (A) move while compaction is running, (B) old owner evicts mid-quiesce, (C) read-after-write follows move?

alex: Yes — propose a 3-stage canary: 1) unit/integ with bloom + manifest, 2) canary cluster with synthetic traffic and random compactions/moves, 3) gradual rollout with checksum alarms enabled.

sre-bot: Canary deploy started for kv-manifest-spike -> canary-evict-cluster. Monitoring: manifest_apply_errors=0, prefill_rate=85%

ops-bot: Scheduling chaos window tomorrow 03:00 UTC for canary cluster. Please add rollback steps to the PR.

lee: Action items: (1) add bloom export on eviction path, (2) add manifest apply idempotency tests, (3) wire `x-prefix-origin` header, (4) add random-prefix checksum probe. I'll take (1) + (4).

alex: I'll prototype the apply loop idempotency and add the manifest proto docs. Maria/Jonathan — can you own the canary test plan?

maria: yep, will draft the chaos scenarios today and ping here.

jonathan: ack, will write the checksum probe and sanity-run it in local sim.

alex: ok team — thanks. putting an RFC follow-up doc on the docs board with these invariants and the test plan.

lee: :thumbsup:
